Description: News ↓ Pull down to refresh Filter by All EVINDIA Out Source EVINDIA Gujarat revises Green Mobility Program: Now pay only 1% RTO on electric vehicles   To accelerate the state's green mobility program and provide substantial financial relief to customers, the Gujarat government has lowered the RTO tax on electric vehicles from 6% to only 1% in a bold step to boost falling EV sales.   The update was included in the Gujarat Budget 2025–2026, which is being praised as a revolutionary step for the economy and environment. Electric vehicle owners are anticipated to benefit between ₹30,000 to ₹1 lakh, depending on the cost of the vehicle, from the 5% tax exemption, which is valid until March 31, 2026.   Earlier, buying an EV for ₹10 lakh required paying ₹60,000 in taxes. However, buyers would now save a flat ₹50,000 by merely paying ₹10,000. The timing of this tax cut is crucial because EV sales have already fallen by over 50% after state subsidies were stopped a year ago.   The new rule ensures transparency and streamlines the registration procedure by limiting the tax reduction to those who register their automobiles online via the Vahan 4.0 site.   Although EV adoption was aided by the previous subsidy of ₹25,000 for two-wheelers and ₹1.5 lakh for four-wheelers under ₹15 lakh, sales plummeted after that support was removed. It is anticipated that the new tax system will reverse that trend.   According to industry analysts, this financial incentive will support sustainable transportation and revive customer enthusiasm, both of which are in line with India's larger objective of lowering carbon emissions. Read full story EVINDIA Jeep Compass EV spotted testing: All you need to know The upcoming fully-electric Compass EV by Jeep, a subsidiary of the Stellantis conglomerate, was spotted testing in Italy a few weeks before its global debut. Earlier, the company had confirmed to launch its second-gen Compass in hybrid, plug-in hybrid, and fully electric versions. The camouflaged prototype spotted seemed to be in the final phase of its testing with some noticeable designs like a faux grille panel with piano black finish up front, flanked by rectangular LED headlamps, a report by Financial Express reported. With a more squared-off frame and a familiar boxy appearance, the new Compass EV highlights its strong and rugged exterior design. In previous teasers, a redesigned seven-slot grille that is expected to include lighting was shown alongside slim LED headlights. However, the grille on the prototype is completely hidden, probably to conceal the final design aspects. In addition,  the front bumper also gets a cooling intake with active flaps to provide aerodynamic sophistication. The test prototype in the most recent spy photos has a completely electric drivetrain, which explains why the exhaust tailpipe is absent. In contrast to the existing Jeep Compass's softly sloping roof, this one looks flatter. There are still unchanged features like the sleek-edged ORVMs, conventional door handles, and squared wheel arches. The EV features new alloy wheels and a clean beltline, making the side profile stand out. However, the new Compass appears longer than the one that is already on the market. According to earlier teaser photos, the taillights have undergone significant modification, including the addition of new C-shaped LED components and the "JEEP" logo. Jeep will transition to a more contemporary STLA Medium architecture and retire the FCA-era platform with the launch of the new generation Compass. This modular framework can support models of different shapes and accommodate a range of powertrains. Jeep hasn't disclosed any precise information on the powertrain specifications, but we anticipate that the Compass EV will have two battery options: 73 kWh and 97 kWh. A dual-motor arrangement will be included with the Compass EV's top-spec dual-motor model. Anirudh Gupta, Chief Finance & Strategy Officer – ex-Grant Thornton Bharat, will oversee finance and capital strategy. “The EV sector has momentum and urgency.
